seoTitle: Westland, MI Personal Injury Lawyer: How a Claim Works, Who You Claim Against, the 18th District Court, and What It Costs
seoDescription: Hurt in Westland? Learn how an injury claim works here: the deadlines; the insurers, the Assigned Claims Plan, and uninsured coverage; claims against landlords, stores, and the mall; the City’s sidewalks and buildings and Wayne County’s roads and Hines Park; nursing home claims; the 18th District and Third Circuit courts; how damages are valued; and the one-third fee cap. ATLAW: 13 years, more than 10,000 cases. Free review. (313) 406-7606.
tagline: What a Westland injury claim involves, from the first week to the check: the deadlines, the courts on Ford Road and in Detroit, who the defendant is, what the claim is worth, what it costs, and what to ask before you hire anyone.

sections.heading: Who the defendant is in Westland

c.v: Westland is a city with its own police and fire departments, sidewalks, and buildings, but many of its major roads, and Hines Park, belong to Wayne County. Much of its housing is in apartment complexes, and it has a regional mall and several nursing homes. Each of those changes who you claim against.

items.v: A landlord must keep the premises and common areas fit for their intended use and in reasonable repair, and comply with health and safety laws (MCL 554.139). That covers stairs, railings, walkways, parking lots, lighting, and snow and ice the landlord controls. Prior complaints, work orders, and incident reports are the evidence. A tenant’s guest may have a premises claim against the landlord as well. See our
The community owner is responsible for the common areas, roads, and lighting it controls, under its lease, the community’s rules, and premises law.

A fall in a store, at the Westland Shopping Center, or in a restaurant or parking lot is a premises claim against the owner, the tenant, or both, depending on who controlled the area. Snow and ice are often handled by a contractor, which can be a separate defendant. Since
(2023), an “open and obvious” hazard such as visible ice goes to comparative fault rather than ending the claim. The deadline is three years. See our
and
pages.
A tenant or customer assaulted at a complex, a store, or a parking lot may have a claim against the owner if it knew of a specific risk and failed to respond reasonably.

c.v: The bar that served the drunk driver.

items.v: A bar, restaurant, or store that served a visibly intoxicated person, or a minor, is liable for the injuries that person causes (MCL 436.1801). The claim needs written notice within 120 days after you hire a lawyer, the drunk driver named and kept in the suit, and suit within two years. See our

c.v: The roads are split three ways.

items.v: MDOT: Ford Road and Michigan Avenue, with written notice of a road defect filed with the Court of Claims within 120 days (MCL 691.1404). Wayne County: Wayne Road, Hines Drive, and other major roads. The City of Westland: the subdivision streets.
A claim against the county or the City requires written notice within 120 days (MCL 691.1402, 691.1404), and the notice must go to the agency that has jurisdiction.

c.v: Sidewalks: the City, and possibly the adjacent owner.

items.v: The City must keep public sidewalks in reasonable repair (MCL 691.1402a). A fall on a broken public sidewalk is a claim against the City, with three limits: the City must have known, or should have known, of the defect at least 30 days before the injury; a defect of less than two inches is presumed not to be actionable; and written notice is due within 120 days.

Even where an ordinance puts sidewalk repair on the adjacent owner, that duty runs to the City and does not by itself make the owner liable to a pedestrian (Levendoski v Geisenhaver, Mich 1965). See our

Hines Park and Hines Drive belong to Wayne County. A crash caused by a defect in Hines Drive is a highway claim against the county, with 120-day notice. An injury in the park itself, on a trail or at a picnic area, generally falls outside every exception to governmental immunity unless it happened in a public building.

An injury caused by a dangerous or defective condition in a public building falls under the public building exception, which requires that the agency knew of the defect and failed to fix it, and written notice within 120 days (MCL 691.1406). That covers City buildings and the buildings of the school districts that serve the city.

c.v: Police and fire are the City’s.

items.v: A crash with a Westland Police car or fire truck is a claim against the City, under the motor vehicle exception to governmental immunity (MCL 691.1405). EMS treatment claims are limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct (MCL 333.20965).
A crash with a SMART bus on Ford Road or Michigan Avenue, or with a school bus, is a claim under the motor vehicle exception. See our
An owner is liable for a bite when the person bitten was lawfully present and did not provoke the dog (MCL 287.351). See our

A claim against a nursing home may be ordinary negligence, with a three-year deadline, or medical malpractice, with two years and a 182-day notice, depending on whether the conduct involved professional judgment. See our

sections.heading: What a Westland claim is worth, and what reduces it

c.v: A claim includes two kinds of damages:

items.v: medical expenses, lost wages, lost earning capacity, and replacement services.
pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life, and disfigurement.

c.v: There is no cap except in medical malpractice. In an auto case, noneconomic damages require a threshold injury: death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement (MCL 500.3135(1)). A serious impairment does not have to be permanent (

, 2010). Vehicle damage up to $3,000 can be recovered from the at-fault driver through the mini tort claim, without a threshold (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)). A premises, dog bite, or dram shop case has no threshold.

Your share of fault reduces the recovery, and above 50 percent it bars noneconomic damages (MCL 600.2959; in auto cases, MCL 500.3135(2)(b)). At exactly 50 percent, you recover half. Where more than one party caused the injury, each defendant generally pays only its own share of fault (MCL 600.2956, 600.6304). That is why the landlord, the management company, and the snow-removal contractor all have to be identified and named. Michigan does not award punitive damages in ordinary injury cases. Exemplary damages for humiliation or outrage are available only in narrow circumstances.
You cannot sue the at-fault party’s liability insurer directly in Michigan. The claim is against the driver, owner, or business, and its insurer defends and pays.
The practical limit is often insurance:

items.v: defaults to $250,000/$500,000 unless the driver chose lower limits, down to the $50,000/$100,000 minimum (MCL 500.3009(1)).

c.v: Michigan caps contingency fees in injury cases at one-third of the net recovery (MCR 8.121). Case costs are advanced by the firm and deducted from the recovery first; the one-third fee is calculated on the remaining amount. You pay nothing up front and nothing if there is no recovery.

The agreement is in writing. Read how costs are handled if the case is lost, because that is where firms differ: filing fees, records, experts, and depositions. A promise that “you pay nothing unless we win” should say whether that includes costs, and whether “win” means the same thing as “settle.” A success rate quoted without saying which cases it counts tells you little.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Westland?

answer.v: Three years for most claims. Several deadlines are much shorter: - one year to notify your no-fault insurer after a crash - 120 days to notify Wayne County or the City of a road or sidewalk defect, or a public agency of a building defect - 120 days for a road-defect notice on Ford Road or Michigan Avenue - 120 days for a dram shop notice after you hire a lawyer, and two years to sue the bar - a 182-day notice and a two-year limit for malpractice

faqs.question: I fell on the stairs in my apartment complex. Who is responsible?

answer.v: Usually the landlord and its management or maintenance company, which must keep common areas in reasonable repair. Report the fall in writing, photograph the stairs and lighting, and keep any earlier complaints you made. Since 2023, the fact that a hazard was visible does not by itself end the claim.

faqs.question: I slipped on ice in a parking lot at the mall or a store. Who is responsible?

answer.v: The owner or tenant that controlled the lot, and often the snow-removal contractor. Photograph the ice and the lot, report the fall, and ask for the incident report.

faqs.question: I was hurt on Hines Drive or in Hines Park. Who do I claim against?

answer.v: For a crash with another driver, the driver, through no-fault and the threshold. For a defect in Hines Drive itself, Wayne County, with written notice within 120 days. For an injury in the park outside a building, governmental immunity usually bars the claim.

faqs.question: The driver who hit me had no insurance. What now?

answer.v: Your own no-fault insurer, a household member’s insurer, or the Assigned Claims Plan pays your medical bills and lost wages regardless of fault. Your pain-and-suffering claim depends on whether you carry uninsured motorist coverage.

faqs.question: Can I sue the other driver’s insurance company?

answer.v: No. In Michigan, the claim is against the driver, and the driver’s insurer defends and pays. Your own no-fault insurer is a separate claim, for your medical bills and lost wages.

faqs.question: What does a Westland personal injury attorney charge?

answer.v: Michigan caps the fee in injury cases at one-third of the net recovery, with no fee if there is no recovery. Case costs are advanced by the firm and deducted only from a recovery.

faqs.question: Where would my Westland case be filed?

answer.v: Claims up to $25,000 go to the 18th District Court on Ford Road. Injury suits over $25,000 go to the Third Judicial Circuit Court in Detroit. Claims against MDOT go to the Court of Claims.

faqs.question: If I was partly at fault, do I still have a claim?

answer.v: Yes, unless you were more than 50 percent at fault, which bars pain-and-suffering damages. Below that, your recovery is reduced by your share, and at exactly 50 percent you recover half. No-fault benefits are paid regardless of fault.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer whose office is in Westland?

answer.v: No. What matters is that the lawyer knows the courts your case will be in, the agencies, insurers, and property owners involved, and will meet you where you are.
